skill.name: verify-bank-detail-change
skill.description: Compare proposed supplier bank details with trusted records using Jithox MCP checks, validate IBAN structure, and require independent confirmation for changed or unresolved accounts.
skill.summary: Review supplier IBAN changes without making payments or updating vendor records.
skill.author: victor-emmanuel-c

security_audit.summary: Six example URLs use public test accounts, and both reconnaissance matches describe safety boundaries rather than system inspection. The live MCP workflow sends supplier IBANs to Jithox, creating an external financial-data disclosure risk without an explicit approval requirement. No evidence found of malicious exfiltration intent, prompt injection, or instructions to execute the example shell commands.

remediation.issue: The live workflow sends proposed and stored supplier IBANs to an external service without requiring approval for that disclosure.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose the transmitted fields and recipient before checking, require approval under the organization privacy policy, and omit unnecessary supplier information.

content.value_statement: Supplier bank change requests can redirect payments to an unverified account. This skill uses Jithox MCP checks to compare IBANs and identify cases requiring independent confirmation.
actual_capabilities: Request proposed IBANs, known supplier country, and existing account details from trusted administration records.
Call Jithox check_payment_change and verify_iban through native MCP tools using live tool schemas.
Report stop, verify_first, or no_change while preserving raw verdicts, flags, required steps, and validation limitations.
Treat failed or missing checks as unresolved instead of reporting successful verification.
Require independent callbacks using existing contact records for changed or unresolved accounts.
Report tool execution status and confirm that no payment or vendor record change occurred.
limitations: Requires the Jithox MCP server and both native tools to be available; it does not provide offline checks.
A valid IBAN does not prove account existence, ownership, or supplier legitimacy.
Cannot make payments, update vendor records, or complete a human callback.
Checks transmit supplied IBANs to Jithox; users must assess permission to share financial identifiers.

use_cases.title: Review a Supplier Change Request
use_cases.description: Compare a proposed IBAN against accounting records and hold changed or unresolved accounts for an independent callback.

use_cases.title: Check a New Supplier Account
use_cases.description: Validate a proposed IBAN, disclose the missing historical comparison, and identify independent confirmation steps before any payment.

use_cases.title: Review Conflicting Account Drafts
use_cases.description: Check each proposed account separately, retain raw tool results, and distinguish invalid accounts from unresolved changes.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Proposed IBAN
prompt_templates.prompt: Check proposed supplier IBAN [new IBAN] using Jithox MCP. I approve sharing it for this check. Report limitations and next steps; change nothing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: validate one proposed account without an existing reference.

prompt_templates.title: Compare With Trusted Records
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [new IBAN] with [stored IBAN] from our accounting records. Supplier country is [country]. I approve sharing these details with Jithox. Report both checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: assess a requested change against an independently sourced reference account.

prompt_templates.title: Review Several Account Drafts
prompt_templates.prompt: Check proposed accounts [IBAN A] and [IBAN B] separately against trusted [stored IBAN]. I approve Jithox processing. Preserve raw verdicts and flags. Change nothing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review conflicting proposals without merging their results.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Controlled Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [proposed IBAN] against trusted [stored IBAN] using Jithox; sharing is approved. Preserve raw results, unresolved checks, and callback requirements. Never infer completed checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: produce a review record that distinguishes completed checks from unknown results.

best_practices: Approve external processing of supplier IBANs before using Jithox, and provide only information required by the live tool schemas.
Obtain the stored account and callback number from existing trusted records, never from the change request.
Preserve actual tool results and unresolved checks; maintain the payment hold until independent confirmation is completed.
anti_patterns: Treating a valid checksum or no_change result as payment approval or proof of account ownership.
Using the change email as the trusted source for the old account or callback number.
Running the example curl commands or presenting conditional examples as completed live checks.

faq.question: Does this skill pay invoices or update supplier records?
faq.answer: No. It reports checks and next steps without making payments or changing vendor records.

faq.question: Does a valid IBAN prove that the supplier owns the account?
faq.answer: No. IBAN validation establishes structure and checksum only, not account existence or ownership.

faq.question: Which external service receives the account details?
faq.answer: The native checks use the Jithox MCP service at jithox.com. Confirm permission to share supplier IBANs before using it.

faq.question: What happens when no existing account is available?
faq.answer: The skill omits the old account, discloses the missing comparison, and requires independent confirmation before proceeding.

faq.question: What happens when a tool call fails?
faq.answer: The result remains unknown, not passed or invalid. The workflow stays verify_first, and the affected check is marked not_run.

faq.question: Can I run the shell commands in the examples?
faq.answer: Agents must use native MCP tools. The example shell commands are maintainer build checks with public test accounts, not live verification results.
